Drops the 'subject to sub-section (3)' limitation and weakens 'proved misbehaviour or incapacity' to 'behaved badly or can't do the job'.
The third party's entitlement to appeal (हकदार है) becomes a statement that he will appeal (अपील करेगा), turning a right into a duty.
Oath before the President or authorised person, the First Schedule form and the signature are all kept.
Good-faith immunity, the acts covered and the scope (Act or rules) are all preserved.
Keeps the override clause, the permissive 'may examine', the public-authority control condition and the no-withholding rule.
A Presidential reference to the Supreme Court under sub-section (1) is described as the Court 'checking a complaint', which is a different procedure.
Drops the clause making Chapter V apply, and renders mediation as 'talk it out'.
Sensory disability condition, the CPIO/SPIO duty to assist and the inspection assistance are all kept.
Partial settlement is recorded and the remaining issues are still heard, by the same three commissions.
'An appeal shall lie' (an appeal is available) becomes 'an appeal must be made', turning a right of appeal into an obligation.
The hundred-day deadline for designating information officers becomes 'one 500 days'.
Keeps 'ordinarily' and both exceptions (disproportionate diversion of resources, harm to the record).
States that the Commission will NOT exercise the powers and functions given to it, reversing the purpose of the provision.
Ninety-day limit, the forum and the sufficient-cause proviso are all kept.
Keeps the subject-to clause, proved misbehaviour or incapacity, the Governor's order, the reference and the Supreme Court report.
Says the Commission will NOT prepare the panel of mediators, reversing the duty, and then contradicts itself by describing how the panel is made.
Drops the State Chief Information Commissioner and several qualifying fields, and turns the closed list of fields into an open 'such as' list.
Sections 35 to 39, the necessary-modifications qualifier and the National Commission are all kept.
Prescribed term, the bar on reappointment and the sixty-five-year age limit are all kept.
Keeps the override of section 7, the forty-day limit, the sub-section (2) representation condition and the written notice.
Drops the information officer who serves the notice and the fact that the ten days run from receipt of that notice, so the time limit has no starting point.
Drops the limitation to orders under sections 20 and 21 and the receipt-of-order start date, and calls an appeal a complaint.
The discretionary power to amend the Schedule becomes a duty ('it must add ... or remove'), contradicting the 'may' in the previous sentence.
Drops 'as soon as practicable' after the year end and reduces the appropriate Government to 'the government', but the annual reporting duty is clear.
The copyright ground is no longer stated as a condition for refusal (the sentence breaks after 'मना कर सकता है'), and the 'other than the State' qualifier is lost.
Drops the application of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and the direction to read references to a decree as references to the order.
Both triggers (admission of a complaint, failed mediation) and the duty to proceed are kept.
Drops the alternative person appointed by the Governor, the First Schedule form of the oath and the requirement to sign it.

Notification, the specified commencement date and the Council's name are all kept.

Both duties, dealing with requests and rendering reasonable assistance, are kept.
